element: Terminal drawer panel (the whole sheet rising from the bottom of the chat column)
geometry: Full pane width. Height = dragHeight ?? settings.terminalHeight (default 260, applied unclamped; drag clamps 140...760). Background UnevenRoundedRectangle with topLeadingRadius 16, topTrailingRadius 16, style .continuous, square bottom corners. Internal layout VStack(spacing: 0): a 38-point tab row then the terminal or the empty state.
colors: Fill Color(white: 0.08) in dark, Color(white: 0.985) in light. Literal greys, not theme tokens; identical to the terminal view's own background so there is no seam.
states: visible: mounted with a move-from-bottom plus opacity transition under Chrome.panelSlide
hidden: unmounted; shells keep running
resizing: height follows the pointer and the chat pane is flagged as live-resizing
thread switching: the visibility animation is nil, so the change is instant
empty: the tab strip is empty and the body shows the empty state
interactions: drag the 8-point top strip to resize
Escape while the composer has focus hides it (after a running turn, before the changes panel)
Escape inside the terminal at the shell prompt hides it
Command-J, the chrome Terminal button, the View menu item and the palette action all toggle it
notes: The persisted height is applied with NO clamp (upstream defect 70). Do not add a load-time clamp; the 140...760 bounds exist only inside the drag handler.

geometry: ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false) wrapping HStack(spacing: 4); .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true). Sits inside the 38-point row, which has .padding(.horizontal, 10) and HStack(spacing: 6) between its groups.
states: overflowing: scrolls horizontally with no visible scrollbar
empty: zero width, so the plus button sits at the left edge
interactions: horizontal scroll or sideways drag scrolls the tabs and does NOT resize the drawer
notes: The source comment at :81-83 records that the whole tab row used to be the resize target and that this was wrong; the drag lives on its own strip precisely so sideways dragging here scrolls.

exact_text: <session title>, which is "Terminal N" for a plain tab or the script's name for a script tab
geometry: HStack(spacing: 6); .padding(.horizontal, 10); .padding(.vertical, 5); capsule background and capsule content shape; 4 points from its neighbours.
typography: .font(.callout) for the chip; the terminal glyph at .caption; the restart and close glyphs at .caption2.weight(.bold).
colors: Selected: foregroundStyle .primary over .primary.opacity(0.08) in a capsule. Unselected: foregroundStyle .secondary over Color.clear.
states: selected: primary text on the 8 percent capsule, plus the close cross visible and clickable
hovered: the close cross becomes visible and clickable
exited shell: whole chip at opacity 0.55, restart button present, tooltip and accessibility label gain the exited wording
running: opacity 1, no restart button
interactions: click anywhere on the capsule to select
hover to reveal the close cross
notes: Tab names are not unique and are never renumbered: closing a middle tab and opening a new one can produce two tabs with the same name.

geometry: Leading item of the tab HStack, 6 points before the title.
colors: Inherits the chip's foreground style (.primary when selected, .secondary otherwise), and the chip's 0.55 opacity when the shell has exited.
states: no state of its own
interactions: none; clicks fall through to the chip
notes: SF Symbol name "terminal". Needs a licensed substitute under UNK-0007.

geometry: Between the glyph and the buttons, 6 points from each.
states: long title: .lineLimit(1) truncates rather than wrapping or growing
interactions: none; clicks fall through to the chip
notes: The title never follows the shell's OSC title sequence: setTerminalTitle is an empty delegate body (TerminalStore.swift:93).

element: Restart button on an exited tab
geometry: Between the title and the close cross, 6 points from each. Present only when the shell has exited, so the chip is narrower while the shell runs.
states: only present when !session.isRunning
interactions: click: terminates the old session and puts a fresh shell in the same tab position, keeping the title and directory and dropping any startup command
notes: Tooltip is exactly "Start a new shell in this tab"; accessibility label is "Restart " followed by the session title. SF Symbol "arrow.clockwise". A restarted script tab does NOT re-run its script.

geometry: Trailing item of the tab HStack, 6 points after the title or the restart button. Always occupies its slot, so the chip width does not change on hover.
states: hidden: opacity 0 and allowsHitTesting false when the tab is neither hovered nor selected, so a click there selects the tab instead
shown: opacity 1 and clickable when hovered or selected
interactions: click: terminates the shell and removes the tab; if it was selected, the selection moves to the LAST remaining tab
notes: Tooltip is exactly "Close terminal"; accessibility label is "Close " followed by the session title. SF Symbol "xmark". There is no confirmation and settings.confirmBeforeDeleting is not consulted. Use opacity 0 with pointer-events none, not display none, or the chip will jump on hover.

geometry: After the tab strip, 6 points from it. Chip button style: .padding(.horizontal, 9), .padding(.vertical, 5), capsule background and content shape.
typography: Glyph at Chrome.iconFont = .system(size: 12, weight: .semibold); the chip style itself sets .font(.callout) on the label.
colors: Chip style, not active: foreground .secondary; fill .primary.opacity(0) at rest, .primary.opacity(0.07) on hover, .primary.opacity(0.12) while pressed, animated with .easeOut(duration: 0.12).
states: rest: no fill
hover: 7 percent primary fill
pressed: 12 percent primary fill
interactions: click: opens a new session in the thread's directory named "Terminal N" and selects it
notes: Tooltip and accessibility label are both exactly "New terminal". SF Symbol "plus".

geometry: At the trailing edge of the row after a Spacer(minLength: 0). Chip button style, same metrics as the plus button.
colors: Chip style, not active, same three fills as UI-TERM-008.
states: rest, hover, pressed as the chip style defines
interactions: click: sets runtime.isTerminalVisible = false; shells keep running
notes: Tooltip is "Hide terminal" plus ShortcutStore.hint, which is a space then the chord in parentheses, or the empty string when the chord is cleared. Accessibility label is always exactly "Hide terminal" with no chord. SF Symbol "chevron.down". Note the chrome row's own button says "Terminal", not "Hide terminal".

geometry: Fills the area below the 38-point tab row, inset .leading 12, .trailing 6, .bottom 6, no extra top inset. The underlying view is created at NSRect(0, 0, 640, 240) and immediately resized to the container.
colors: Dark: background white 0.08, foreground white 0.9. Light: background white 0.985, foreground white 0.12. Caret = Chrome.accentNSColor (theme accent, or the system control accent for System, Light and Dark). Selection background = that accent at 0.3 alpha. The 16 ANSI colours are SwiftTerm 1.20.0 defaults and are not configured anywhere in the source.
states: focused: takes the keyboard once when the drawer is opened
exited: keeps showing its final scrollback; the tab dims
window live-resizing: autoresizing parked, frame synced at most every 50 ms, one final sync on release
interactions: all keyboard input goes to the shell
Option is sent as Meta (optionAsMetaKey = true)
Escape at the shell prompt with no modifiers closes the drawer and is swallowed; Escape with a foreground program running reaches that program
mouse selection uses SwiftTerm's own handling
notes: There is no user setting anywhere for terminal font, size, cursor style or palette. The view is a single long-lived object reparented between containers, never rebuilt, so scrollback survives tab and thread switches.

geometry: Overlaid at .top, full width, .frame(height: 8). Covers the empty band above the tabs, not the tab row itself.
colors: Transparent; only the grip bar is drawn.
states: hover: grip widens to 28 and fades to opacity 0.6 over 0.18 s ease-out
dragging: grip stays shown even if the pointer leaves the strip
rest: grip 12 wide at opacity 0
interactions: pointer over the strip shows the ns-resize cursor before any press
press and drag up to grow the drawer, down to shrink it; clamped 140...760
release commits the height to the persisted key "terminalHeight"
a click with no movement still commits the same value
notes: AppKit y increases upward, so the source's positive delta means dragging up. On Windows and in the DOM the sign must be inverted. mouseUp applies one final onChange before onEnd, so the release pixel counts.

geometry: Height 2.5, corner radius 1.25 (height / 2), width 12 at rest and 28 when shown, centred horizontally and vertically in the 8-point strip.
colors: NSColor.labelColor resolved in the current appearance, repainted on every effective-appearance change.
states: rest: width 12, opacity 0
shown (hover or drag): width 28, opacity 0.6
transitions animate over 0.18 s with an ease-out curve; layout-driven updates are applied with animations disabled
interactions: none of its own; it is a hover affordance for UI-TERM-011
notes: The same affordance as the sidebar's edge grip (the source names SidebarResizeHandleView); porting/extracts/chrome-design-tokens.md:358 confirms SidebarResizeHandleView.Grip.duration is also 0.18.

exact_text: No shell open in this thread
geometry: Centred in the area below the tab row, 10 points above the button, inside a VStack framed to maxWidth .infinity and maxHeight .infinity.
states: shown only when the thread has zero sessions and the drawer is open
interactions: none
notes: Reached by closing every tab; the drawer deliberately stays open rather than hiding itself.

geometry: 10 points below the label, .controlSize(.small).
typography: Inherited from the glass button style at small control size.
colors: .buttonStyle(.glass) - the macOS Liquid Glass style, which the port approximates under UNK-0004.
states: always enabled while the empty state is shown
interactions: click: opens a session exactly as the plus button does
notes: Note the wording differs from the plus button's "New terminal" tooltip; both open the same thing.

geometry: Inside a ChromeCapsule, before a ChromeDivider and the Changes button, in the trailing group of the chrome row.
colors: Draws in its active state exactly while runtime.isTerminalVisible is true.
states: active: drawer visible
inactive: drawer hidden
interactions: click: toggles runtime.isTerminalVisible
notes: Tooltip is "Terminal" plus the chord hint, so "Terminal (Command-J)" by default. This is a different string from the drawer's own "Hide terminal" chevron tooltip; the two must not be unified. SF Symbol "terminal".

geometry: Inside the leading ChromeCapsule, after OpenInMenu and a ChromeDivider; present only when the thread resolves to a project.
states: absent (not disabled) when the thread has no project
interactions: click: opens the scripts popover
notes: Tooltip is exactly "Run a project script". SF Symbol "play".

geometry: PopoverSectionHeader at the top of the popover; omitted entirely when the project has no scripts.
states: omitted when project.scripts is empty
interactions: none
notes: When it is omitted, so are the script rows and the divider, leaving only the add row.

geometry: One PopoverItem per script, in the project's stored order.
states: no disabled state; every script is runnable
interactions: click: runs that script in a new terminal tab and shows the drawer
notes: The row's glyph is the script's own symbol, which comes from droppy-code.json's icon field mapped through the five-entry table, or "play". There is no way to change the symbol from the UI.

exact_text: Add a script… (when the project has no scripts) / Edit scripts… (when it has at least one)
geometry: The last row, after a PopoverDivider when any scripts exist.
states: empty project: reads "Add a script" plus U+2026 with the plus glyph
non-empty project: reads "Edit scripts" plus U+2026 with the pencil glyph
interactions: click: presents the Project scripts sheet
notes: The ellipsis is the single character U+2026, not three full stops. SF Symbols "plus" and "pencil".

geometry: .padding(20); .frame(width: 580, height: 460); children in a VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14). Presentation corner radius Chrome.windowCornerRadius, with a WindowBackdrop at the user's backdropOpacity behind it.
colors: The app's own window glass, so the sheet reads as one window's worth of chrome rather than a system sheet.
states: fixed size; it does not grow with the number of scripts, the list scrolls instead
interactions: Escape triggers the Cancel button's cancel role
notes: The comment at :1460-1462 explains the backdrop is painted here because the Settings window's own backdrop is not behind a sheet.

geometry: First child, leading-aligned, 14 points above the description.
states: static
interactions: none

exact_text: Scripts run in a terminal at the project root. Droppy Code also picks up scripts from droppy-code.json.
geometry: Second child, leading-aligned, 14 points below the title and above the list.
states: static
interactions: none
notes: Two sentences, both with full stops. Contains the product name, which is the one string in this area affected by the owner-approved rename; the source wording is the specification until the owner records the substitution. Note the claim is slightly inaccurate in the source: scripts are picked up from droppy-code.json only when the project is first added, never again.

geometry: ChromeCard with .padding(14) inside; contents in VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8); cards 10 points apart inside a ScrollView with .frame(minHeight: 220).
states: incomplete (blank or space-only command): the command field gains the danger outline and Save is disabled
interactions: edit the two fields, toggle the checkbox, delete with the trash button
notes: There is no drag handle: the order is fixed by the underlying array, and the first card is the top script that Command-R runs.

geometry: Leading item of the card's first HStack, beside the trash button. .textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder).
states: a blank name is allowed and does not block saving
interactions: type to rename; the change is local until Save
notes: Only the command is validated. A script saved with an empty name shows as an empty menu row.

geometry: Trailing item of the card's first HStack. .buttonStyle(.borderless), role .destructive.
states: always enabled
interactions: click: removes the card from the local list immediately, with no confirmation
notes: SF Symbol "trash". settings.confirmBeforeDeleting is NOT consulted here. Cancel still restores the script, because the removal is local until Save.

geometry: Second item of the card's VStack, 8 points below the name row and above the checkbox. .textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder). Incomplete overlay: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6, style: .continuous).strokeBorder(Chrome.danger.opacity(0.65), lineWidth: 1).
colors: Rounded-border field default; the error outline is the theme danger hue at 0.65 opacity, 1 point wide.
states: incomplete: the command is empty after trimming spaces, so the danger outline is drawn and Save is disabled
complete: no overlay
interactions: type the shell command; the text is used verbatim with no quoting or escaping
notes: The trim is trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces), not .whitespacesAndNewlines, so a tab-only command counts as complete. The comment at :1689-1690 records that such a script used to be dropped on save without a word.

element: Run when a worktree is created checkbox
exact_text: Run when a worktree is created
geometry: Last item of the card's VStack, 8 points below the command field. .toggleStyle(.checkbox).
states: off by default for a new script and for an imported script without the field
interactions: click: flips the flag; the change is local until Save
notes: Flagged scripts run in the NEW WORKTREE path, not the project path, when a worktree is created for a thread.

geometry: Leading item of the footer HStack, before the Spacer.
states: always enabled
interactions: click: appends a card named "New script" with an empty command, which immediately disables Save
notes: Label("Add script", systemImage: "plus"), so the glyph and text are one label.

geometry: After the Spacer, before Save.
states: always enabled
interactions: click or Escape: dismisses the sheet and discards every edit, including deletions
notes: role: .cancel, which is what makes Escape dismiss the sheet.

geometry: Trailing item of the footer HStack.
states: disabled while any script's command is blank after trimming spaces
enabled otherwise
interactions: click: replaces the project's whole scripts array with the edited list and dismisses
notes: Tooltip is exactly "Every script needs a command." while disabled and exactly "Save these scripts" while enabled; note only the first has a full stop. The save is a wholesale replacement and never merges.

geometry: In CommandGroup(after: .sidebar), after "Command palette" and before "Toggle changes".
states: disabled when model.selectedThreadID is nil
interactions: click or the chord (Command-J by default): toggles the selected thread's drawer

exact_text: Run <first script name> (when one exists) / Run top script (when none does)
geometry: After "Next thread" and before the numbered "Thread N" items.
states: disabled when model.topScript is nil, which covers both no selected thread and a project with no scripts
interactions: click or the chord (Command-R by default): runs the project's first script in a new terminal tab and shows the drawer
notes: The title is composed as "Run " plus the script name, so a script called "Release" gives the item "Run Release".

geometry: Appended to the actions list only when a thread is selected, before the changes and finish rows.
states: absent (not disabled) when no thread is selected
the trailing chord label is omitted entirely when the chord has been cleared
interactions: run: toggles the selected thread's drawer
notes: SF Symbol "terminal". Item id is "terminal".

screen: Settings, Shortcuts page, Window and panels section
exact_text: Toggle terminal / Shows or hides the thread's terminal.
geometry: In the section titled "Window and panels".
states: customized: the row is marked as overridden
cleared: a stored empty chord means the shortcut answers to nothing and every hint that showed it becomes the empty string
interactions: record a new chord; the refusal rules apply (a modifier-only chord, a text-typing key without Command, Control or Option, a key menus cannot use, a reserved chord, or a chord another command already owns)
notes: Default chord is keyCode 38 with Command, which is Command-J. The description's trailing full stop is part of the string.

exact_text: Run top script / Runs the first project script in the selected thread's terminal.
geometry: In the section titled "Threads".
states: customized or cleared as for UI-TERM-034
interactions: record a new chord under the same refusal rules
notes: Default chord is keyCode 15 with Command, which is Command-R. The description's trailing full stop is part of the string.
